name: Calendly
summary: The app connects to Calendly using OAuth 2.0. You must register your own OAuth app through the Calendly Developer Portal and configure its redirect URI to match the Composio callback. You then supply your client credentials in the Composio dashboard to enable OAuth-based authentication and access to the Calendly API.
decision: You must register your own Calendly OAuth application by visiting the Calendly Developer Portal, choosing to create a new app, specifying required fields—critically including the redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback—then copying the generated client ID and client secret into the Composio dashboard. Composio requires you to use your own developer authentication. Although Composio guides the configuration, the Calendly developer portal is the place where you create and manage the OAuth app.

redirect_uri.note: Must be set as the Redirect URI in your Calendly OAuth app, with https, no trailing slash, and must exactly match in Calendly and Composio.

prerequisites.title: Calendly Developer account
prerequisites.body: Sign up for a Calendly developer account using Github or Google via the developer portal.

prerequisites.title: Composio account
prerequisites.body: You need access to the Composio dashboard to finish the OAuth configuration.

steps.title: Sign in to Calendly Developer Portal
steps.body: Visit https://developer.calendly.com/ and sign in or register for a developer account using Github or Google.

steps.title: Create New OAuth Application
steps.body: Click 'My Apps' and then 'Create New App'. Provide the app name, select 'Web' as the kind of app, and pick your environment (Sandbox for development, Production to go live).

steps.title: Configure Redirect URI
steps.body: Set the redirect URI for your OAuth app to: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Ensure it uses https, with no trailing slash, and exactly matches the value used in your Composio configuration.
steps.note: This step is critical for the OAuth callback to succeed.

steps.title: Select Required Scopes
steps.body: Choose the OAuth scopes necessary for your integration. Common scopes include: default, users:read, events:read, event_types:read, webhook_subscriptions:write.

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Client Secret
steps.body: After app creation, Calendly will display the Client ID and Client Secret. Copy and save them safely, as you cannot view the secret again.
steps.note: Keep these confidential; you'll need them in the next step.

steps.title: Configure Authentication in Composio
steps.body: In the Composio dashboard (https://platform.composio.dev/), begin creating a new Auth Config for Calendly. Set authentication type to OAuth2 and enable 'Use your own developer authentication'. Paste your Client ID and Client Secret into the Manage Auth Config section.

steps.title: Save and Store Auth Config ID
steps.body: After creating your Auth Config, copy the generated Auth Config ID from Composio and store it securely.
steps.note: You use this Auth Config ID in your code to authenticate requests.

human_actions.title: Register Calendly developer account
human_actions.body: A human must sign up for a Calendly developer account if they haven't already.

human_actions.title: Create and configure OAuth app in developer portal
human_actions.body: A human fills in all required app registration fields, including redirect URI, in the Calendly developer portal.

human_actions.title: Manually input credentials into Composio
human_actions.body: A human must copy the Client ID and Client Secret from Calendly and enter them in Composio.
